simple.meaning: תָּקַן (tâqan) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to equalize , i.e. straighten (intransitive or transitive); figuratively, to compose.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Ecclesiastes, beginning at Ecclesiastes 1:15. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּקַן (H8626).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

firstOccurrence.englishText: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.

timeline.evidenceText: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked?
Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.

definitions.full: H8626. taqan [ תָּקַן ] verb become straight (Late Hebrew תִּקֵּן arrange, put right ; Ecclus 47:9 תיקן set in order ; Assyrian takânu , be well ordered , especially Pi`el as Late Hebrew; Aramaic be established, firm , Pa`el , תֵּקֵּין fix, arrange, prepare , etc.; Palmyrene Pa`el erect ); — Qal Infinitive construct לִתְקֹן Eccl 1:15 (opposed to מְעֻוָּת bent ). Pi`el Infinitive construct לְתַקֵּן Eccl 7:13 make straight (opposed to עִוָּה ); Perfect 3masculine singular תִּקֵּן 12:9 put straight, arrange in order (proverbs). [ תְּקַן ] verb be in order ( ᵑ7 Syriac; Biblical Hebrew (late)); — Hoph`al Perfect 1singular הָתְקְנֵת (W CG 225 ) Dan 4:33 I was established , עַל of kingdom.
